reason: The text depicts the Egyptian elite—particularly Pharaoh, his officials, and military leadership—extremely unfavorably. Pharaoh is characterized as having a 'hardened heart,' and he and his servants are portrayed as self-interested oppressors who regret their decision to release the Israelites only because they have lost their labor force. They pursue the Israelites to recapture them, and this pursuit results in their complete destruction in the Red Sea. The narrative emphasizes their defeat and the futility of their opposition to God's will. While Moses (an Israelite leader) is also elite and portrayed favorably, the dominant elite figures in this passage—the Egyptian elite—are consistently depicted in a decidedly negative light.
